upstream_output.text: Lantern Notes is a small, offline-first note store for field teams. It keeps notes on the device and synchronises them when a connection is available.
Status: beta. The storage format may still change between minor versions.
Download the archive for your platform from the releases page.
Unpack it into a directory of your choice:
Run lantern init once, then add notes:

lantern add "Check the north gate"
lantern list --since 7d
Command Purpose Since init Create a notebook 1.0 add Append a note 1.0 sync Exchange changes with a peer 1.2
Please read CONTRIBUTING before opening a pull request, and follow the code of conduct.
Lantern Notes is released under the Apache License 2.0.
All notable changes to this project are documented here. The format follows the Keep a Changelog convention and the project uses semantic versioning.
Export notes as Markdown with lantern export --format md.
Optional end-to-end encryption for synchronised notebooks (see the encryption guide).
Sync no longer duplicates notes whose titles differ only in case.
Timestamps in the list output now use the device time zone.
Breaking: the configuration file moved from ~/.lantern to ~/.config/lantern/config.toml.
Raised the minimum SQLite version to 3.35.
Reject notebook archives containing absolute paths (advisory).
This guide explains how to record a survey site. Read it before your first visit; the checklist at the end is the minimum for a valid record.
a printed copy of the site map.
Keep the map in the waterproof sleeve.
Stand at the marker and wait for a fix. The receiver shows FIX when it is ready.
latitude and longitude in decimal degrees;
The receiver writes a log line like this:
Tip: if the fix takes more than five minutes, move away from trees and try again.
Nested note: tall buildings cause the same problem.

Temperatures use °C, distances use metres, and the elevation symbol is Δh. Survey teams in other regions record names in their own scripts: 東京 (Tokyo), القاهرة (Cairo) and Ελλάδα (Greece). Use the combining form é only when the source uses it. Team emoji such as 👩‍🔬 are allowed in comments. Line one ends with a hard break\ line two continues the paragraph.
See the glossary and the https://example.org/survey/faq page for help, or write to survey-help@example.org. Use & rather than "and" in site codes, and © notices belong in the footer.
